messages.subject: Barrick Global Affairs | Operating-side government and stakeholder leadership
messages.body:
Dear Corporate Secretary,

Please place this distinct Global Affairs follow-up before Mr. Woo Lee, Chief Global Affairs Officer.

Barrick's decision to place Global Affairs on the Executive Committee sends a clear signal about the strategic weight of government and sovereign relationships across the portfolio. Your remit is unusually close to the work I have built my career around, but from the operating side of a multinational mining business.

The strongest contribution I see is at the point where global government strategy meets country execution. Sovereign relationships create value when local regulatory pathways, community expectations, operating commitments, social-performance priorities and executive decisions stay aligned. A leader who understands those interfaces from inside an operating mine can help turn high-level relationships into consistent institutional outcomes.

I serve as Liaison Director, Social Responsibility Department at AGM Inc., part of Zijin Mining Group. My mandate spans government and regulatory relations, ESG and social performance, corporate affairs, strategic partnerships, executive advisory and cross-functional issue management. I work directly across ministries, regulators, communities and internal operating teams, including environment, HSE, legal, finance, HR, procurement, security and technical functions.

A related executive introduction was sent to Barrick's corporate office on 30 September, so I am not restarting that conversation. I am writing to you with a distinct Global Affairs proposition: where Barrick needs stronger country-level institutional execution, stakeholder strategy or government-relations leadership, I believe my operating experience warrants a closer look. I have attached a CV focused specifically on that fit.

Kind regards,
Ragunauth Ramsaroop
Liaison Director, Social Responsibility Department | AGM Inc.
